description: A single-panel dual-ordinate line plot titled "Elastic parameters for Fe-Al alloys". The abscissa is "Aluminium content (%)" spanning 0-40 (ticks 0, 10, 20, 30, 40); the left ordinate is "Stiffness constants (GPa)" (0-140) and the right ordinate "Anisotropy factor" (2-7). Three annotated data series are plotted. C44 (filled circles, solid line, left axis) lies above the 120 GPa gridline across most of the range, rising to its highest values near 25-28% Al. (C11 - C12)/2 (filled squares, solid line, left axis) falls from between the 40 and 60 GPa gridlines at 0% Al to a minimum at about the 20 GPa gridline near 30% Al, then rises again. The anisotropy factor A (open triangles, dashed line, right axis) climbs steeply from close to the 2 gridline at 0% Al, shows a shoulder near 25% Al, reaches a maximum between the 6 and 7 gridlines around 28-30% Al, then falls toward the 4 gridline at 40% Al. The text labels "C44", "(C11 - C12)/2" and "A" sit beside their curves. The figure demonstrates that the elastic-anisotropy maximum of Fe-Al alloys coincides with the 26-30% Al range.
measured_quantities: elastic stiffness constants C44 and (C11 - C12)/2 (GPa)

observations.observation: The figure is a single plot with two ordinate axes: left 'Stiffness constants (GPa)' (0-140) and right 'Anisotropy factor' (2-7), both against the abscissa 'Aluminium content (%)' (0-40).
Three series are plotted: C44 (filled circles, solid line), (C11 - C12)/2 (filled squares, solid line) and the anisotropy factor A (open triangles, dashed line).
The C44 curve stays above the 120 GPa gridline over most of the composition range and reaches its highest values near 25-28% Al.
The (C11 - C12)/2 curve decreases from between the 40 and 60 GPa gridlines at 0% Al to a minimum near the 20 GPa gridline at about 30% Al, then rises again toward 40% Al.

The anisotropy factor A (dashed line, open triangles, right axis) rises steeply from close to the 2 gridline at 0% Al to a maximum between the 6 and 7 gridlines at about 28-30% Al, then falls toward the 4 gridline at 40% Al.
The A curve shows a shoulder/local upturn near 25% Al before its main maximum at ~28-30% Al.
The text labels 'C44', '(C11 - C12)/2' and 'A' are printed next to their respective curves.
The caption states the figure shows the variation of elastic stiffness constants and anisotropy factor as a function of Al content.
The caption states the data are taken from Refs. [22,23].
The citing text states the Zener anisotropy factor is defined as A = 2C44/(C11 - C12), with C11, C12 and C44 being stiffness constants.
The citing text states Fe3Al alloys have an extremely high degree of elastic anisotropy.
The citing text attributes the increased anisotropy to both an increase in C44 and a fall in (C11 - C12)/2.
The citing text states that addition of 25-30% Al leads to the onset of long range order, changing single dislocations to superdislocations.
The citing text states the change of elastic behaviour over the 25-30% Al range parallels the work-hardening behaviour and needs further examination.
